title: Aligned-pair scan loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with oracle, let $x,w$ be finite bit strings, and let $r$ and $\ell$ be distinct registers. Choose an oracle index $j$, program states $\mathrm{scan},\mathrm{first},\mathrm{fail},\mathrm{done}$ and states $\mathrm{test}(b),\mathrm{read}(b)$ for each bit $b$, and states $\mathrm{advance}(k,i)$ for $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and natural numbers $i$. Suppose the scan instruction compares registers $r$ and $\ell$, the first instruction calls oracle $j$ on the whole input and the word in register $r$, each test compares those registers, and each read calls the oracle on that same input, branching as specified by the bit being tested; each advance instruction increments register $r$ and proceeds to the next advance state. Assume the four advance states at offset $\mathrm{stride}$ lead respectively to $\mathrm{test}(\mathrm{false})$, $\mathrm{test}(\mathrm{true})$, $\mathrm{scan}$, and $\mathrm{done}$; also assume $0<\mathrm{stride}$, every register value in the initial vector $v$ is at most $B$, $v(\ell)=v(r)+\mathrm{stride}|w|$, and for every $i<|w|$ the oracle answer on $\langle x,\mathrm{bits}(v(r)+\mathrm{stride}i)\rangle$ is the $i$-th bit of $w$ (defaulting to false past the end). Then the program reaches a failure state with register $r$ increased by $\mathrm{stride}t$ for some $t\le |w|$ if the aligned-pair parser rejects $w$; if it parses $w$ as $(a,b)$, it reaches $\mathrm{done}$ with register $r$ increased by $\mathrm{stride}(2|a|+2)$. In either case, throughout the finite run every intermediate configuration satisfies the program's precondition—equality tests use distinct registers, input-word tests occur on valid encodings, and call argument lists have no repetitions—and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ is a register program and $\mathrm{oracle}$ is an oracle
The stated scan, first, test, read, advance, and terminal instruction equations hold
$v$ is a register vector with every value at most $B$
For every $i<|w|$, the specified oracle query returns the $i$-th bit of $w$
caveat: The statement includes the exact state-transition equations and the program precondition encoded by the supplied definitions; these have been summarized in prose.
